record.paper_title: Current work and open problems in the numerical analysis of Volterra functional equations with vanishing delays
record.original_question: Suppose the answers to the asymptotic-stability questions for the proportional-delay case θ(t)=qt, 0<q<1, are known. Do those answers remain valid when the delay is replaced by a nonlinear function θ satisfying the paper's conditions (N1)–(N3)?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 4.3 Suppose that answers to Open Problems 4.1 and 4.2 are known (for the delay function θ(t) = qt, 0 <q< 1). Do they remain valid for nonlinear θ satisfying conditions (N1)–(N3)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the linear Volterra functional equation with vanishing delay
   y(t) = a(t) y(t) + b(t) y(θ(t)) + (V y)(t) + (V_θ y)(t) + f(t),  t ∈ [0,∞),
or, in the differential case,
   y'(t) = a(t) y(t) + b(t) y(θ(t)) + (V y)(t) + (V_θ y)(t) + f(t),  y(0) = y_0,
where (V y)(t) = ∫_0^t K(t,s) y(s) ds and (V_θ y)(t) = ∫_0^{θ(t)} K_θ(t,s) y(s) ds, with sufficiently smooth coefficients and kernels, and θ:[0,∞)→[0,∞) is a vanishing delay function.

Assume that θ satisfies the following conditions:
 (N1) θ ∈ C([0,∞)) ∩ C^1((0,∞)), θ(0) = 0, and 0 < θ(t) < t for all t > 0;
 (N2) θ'(t) > 0 for all t > 0, and θ'(t) is bounded on every compact subinterval of (0,∞);
 (N3) lim_{t→0+} θ(t)/t = q for some constant q ∈ (0,1), so that θ behaves asymptotically like a proportional (pantograph-type) delay near 0.

For the special proportional case θ(t) = q t with 0 < q < 1, suppose that complete answers are known to the following two asymptotic-stability questions:
 (P1) Characterize the values of the mesh parameters and the coefficients (a, b, kernels) for which the exact solution y(t) → 0 as t → ∞.
 (P2) Characterize the values of the mesh parameters and method parameters (e.g., collocation parameters on a quasi-geometric or uniform mesh) for which the piecewise polynomial collocation approximation u_h(t) → 0 as t → ∞, and determine whether this asymptotic stability is preserved by the fully discretized scheme.

Question: Do the answers obtained for θ(t) = q t in (P1) and (P2) remain valid, without modification, when θ is replaced by an arbitrary nonlinear delay function satisfying (N1)–(N3)? If not, determine the precise modifications required.
artifact.category_tag: Numerical analysis of delay Volterra equations
artifact.status_search_result: Searches indicate that even for the proportional-delay case θ(t)=qt, the asymptotic stability of collocation solutions on uniform meshes for pantograph-type Volterra functional equations is still listed as an open problem in recent surveys and follow-up work. Since the nonlinear-delay version is contingent on these proportional-delay answers (which are not yet fully established), the extension to nonlinear θ satisfying (N1)–(N3) likewise remains open.

status_evidence.title: Current work and open problems in the numerical analysis of Volterra functional equations with vanishing delays
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems on asymptotic stability of collocation solutions for pantograph-type Volterra functional equations and their extension to nonlinear vanishing delays.
status_evidence.claim: The asymptotic stability questions, including their extension to nonlinear vanishing delays, are stated as open problems.

status_evidence.title: On the asymptotic stability of Volterra functional equations with vanishing delays
status_evidence.snippet: Studies asymptotic stability for Volterra functional equations with vanishing delays; results focus on specific cases and do not fully resolve the nonlinear-delay extension.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work addresses asymptotic stability for vanishing delays but does not fully settle the nonlinear-delay case under conditions (N1)–(N3).

status_evidence.title: Analysis of continuous collocation solutions for nonlinear functional equations with vanishing delays
status_evidence.snippet: Analyzes collocation methods for nonlinear functional equations with vanishing delays, focusing on convergence rather than full asymptotic-stability characterization.
status_evidence.claim: Further work treats nonlinear vanishing delays for collocation, but the asymptotic-stability extension parallel to the proportional case is not completely resolved.
